## A. Builtin coverage

Inventory: `builtins` of the reference. Each `name/arity` runs on eight inputs under `try ... catch "E"`; error wording is the error-probe suite's job.

jq-1.7.1 builtins: 203 match, 4 differ, 0 not implemented, 11 not probed.

| Builtin | Status | Ledger |
|---------|--------|--------|
| `get_jq_origin/0` | differs | host-dependent: Prints the directory of the running binary, so the two tools differ by installation path alone. |
| `strflocaltime/1` | differs | reference-crash: Same jq 1.7.1 assertion abort on a non-string format as strftime/1. |
| `strftime/1` | differs | reference-crash: jq 1.7.1 aborts (`Assertion failed: JVP_HAS_KIND(j, JV_KIND_STRING)`, jv.c:1370) on a non-string format; succinctly reports a catchable error. |
| `strptime/1` | differs | host-dependent: On `"a" | strptime(.)` the weekday of 1900-00-00 is 6 in jq 1.7.1 on macOS, `[…,8,367]` on glibc, and `[…,0,-1]` in succinctly; the value is platform-libc dependent (#5340). |

Not probed: `debug/0` (writes to stderr), `debug/1` (writes to stderr), `env/0` (host environment), `halt/0` (ends the process), `halt_error/0` (ends the process), `halt_error/1` (ends the process), `input/0` (consumes the probe's own input), `inputs/0` (consumes the probe's own input), `now/0` (non-deterministic), `stderr/0` (writes to stderr), `until/2` (does not terminate on the default argument).

| Probe | jq exit | succinctly exit | Ledger |
|-------|---------|-----------------|--------|
| `version` | 0 | 0 | by-design: `--version` names the tool (`succinctly jq ... 0.8.0`), not jq's version token. |
| `help-exit` | 0 | 0 | by-design: `-h` prints succinctly's own usage text. |
| `help-long-exit` | 0 | 0 | by-design: `--help` prints succinctly's own usage text. |
| `build-configuration` | 0 | 0 | by-design: `--build-configuration` describes succinctly's build, not jq's configure line. |
| `debug-dump-disasm` | 0 | 2 | by-design: succinctly has no bytecode to disassemble; the flag is rejected (exit 2). |
| `debug-trace` | 0 | 2 | by-design: succinctly has no bytecode to trace; the flag is rejected (exit 2). |
| `locale-strptime-ampm-en-us` | 0 | 0 | host-dependent: Same platform-dependent weekday as `locale-strptime-ampm-c`, under `en_US.UTF-8`. |
| `locale-strptime-en-de-de` | 0 | 5 | host-dependent: `"Thursday, March 05 2015" | strptime("%A, %B %d %Y")` under `de_DE.UTF-8`: glibc's `strptime` reads the `C` locale's English names as well as the locale's own, so a glibc jq 1.7.1 answers where the macOS pin's libc and succinctly exit 5 (docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md, "glibc `jq` under a locale, measured"). Only a Linux host that has `de_DE` shows it: without the locale both tools fall back to `C` and agree. |
| `locale-strptime-en-tr-tr` | 0 | 5 | host-dependent: `"Thursday, March 05 2015" | strptime("%A, %B %d %Y")` under `tr_TR.UTF-8`: the same glibc behaviour as `locale-strptime-en-de-de`, reading the `C` locale's English names beside the locale's own. Only a Linux host that has `tr_TR` shows it. |
| `locale-strptime-ampm-tr-tr` | 0 | 5 | host-dependent: Same platform-dependent weekday as `locale-strptime-ampm-c`, under `tr_TR.UTF-8`, on a host without that locale (it falls back to `C`). A host that has the locale matches: neither tool parses `PM` there, and both exit 5. |
| `locale-strptime-ampm-c` | 0 | 0 | host-dependent: `"11:30 PM" | strptime("%I:%M %p")`: the weekday (element 6) is 6 in jq 1.7.1 on macOS and 0 in succinctly. It is the platform libc's weekday and yearday of a format that sets no date (docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md, "`strptime` weekday and yearday of a format that sets no date", #5340, #5383): jq's macOS build derives it from the unset date (`1900-01-00`) with its own `set_tm_wday()`, glibc leaves jq's `8`/`367` sentinels, and succinctly answers the date's own weekday. `"12"|strptime("%H")` and `"3"|strptime("%d")` differ the same way. |
| `strftime-negative-year-y` | 0 | 0 | host-dependent: `[-5,0,1,0,0,0,0,0] | strftime("%y|%C|%D")` is `05|-0|01/01/05` in jq 1.7.1 on macOS (the libc's `_yconv`: the remainder's absolute value, and `-0` for a century of 0) and succinctly follows it. A glibc jq prints `95|-1|01/01/95` (the floored remainder and quotient), as it prints `%Y` of year -5 as `-5` where the pin prints `-005` (docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md, "negative years"). Measured on Ubuntu 22.04 with a source-built jq 1.7.1. |
| `strftime-negative-year-century` | 0 | 0 | host-dependent: `[-101,0,1,0,0,0,0,0] | strftime("%y|%C")` is `01|-1` in jq 1.7.1 on macOS and succinctly follows it; a glibc jq prints `99|-2` (the floored remainder and quotient). Same cause as `strftime-negative-year-y`. |

## C. Input conformance: JSONTestSuite

Accepting is exit 0. `y_` must be accepted, `n_` rejected, `i_` is implementation-defined. `succinctly` as shipped semi-indexes and validates little; `--validate` is strict RFC 8259.

| Class | Cases | jq accepts | succinctly accepts | succinctly --validate accepts |
|-------|-------|------------|--------------------|-------------------------------|
| y_ | 95 | 95 | 95 | 95 |
| n_ | 188 | 25 | 39 | 0 |
| i_ | 35 | 25 | 31 | 11 |

The ledger lists a case only when `--validate` breaks its `y_`/`n_` expectation or the two tools print different values for an input both accept; jq itself accepts 25 `n_` cases.

## B. Grammar-based differential fuzzing

`scripts/jq-grammar-fuzz.py` generates jq programs and documents from a typed grammar under a fixed seed, so a run covers the same programs every time. Exit status, stdout and the fault's class (the first stderr line without position or value) must match jq 1.7.1's. A program jq does not compile, or that times out, is skipped: the generator's mistake, not evidence. `answered` counts the programs both tools ran to a result; those carry the signal.

| Seed | Programs | Agree | Answered | Skipped | Divergence signatures |
|------|----------|-------|----------|---------|-----------------------|
| 1 | 2000 | 1970 | 766 | 30 | 0 |
| 2 | 2000 | 1959 | 785 | 41 | 0 |
| 3 | 2000 | 1967 | 761 | 33 | 0 |

No divergence found.

## B. Oracle sweeps

Each `scripts/jq-*-sweep.*` script listed in `manifest.toml`'s `[[sweep]]` runs its own grid through both tools and judges its own rows, including the residuals it expects; the runner reads only its exit status (1: a divergence the script does not expect). A diverging sweep is ledgered as `sweep:<id>`, so a second divergence in a listed sweep does not change the outcome.

## F. Robustness and resource limits

Each probe has a 10 s deadline. Class: `ok`, `error` (non-zero exit), `crash` (signal or panic), `timeout`. Stdout and exit status must match jq's; a crash or hang of succinctly is listed even when jq does the same.

| Area | Probes | Agree |
|------|--------|-------|
| errors | 9 | 9 |
| generators | 13 | 13 |
| memory | 12 | 9 |
| nesting | 17 | 17 |
| numbers | 9 | 8 |
| pipe | 3 | 3 |
| recursion | 7 | 6 |
| regex | 7 | 6 |
| strings | 9 | 9 |
| wide | 11 | 11 |

| Probe | jq | succinctly | Ledger |
|-------|----|-------------|--------|
| `recursion-depth-10000` | ok 0 (5928 ms) | timeout signal (10008 ms) | by-design: A user-defined function recursing 10000 deep: jq answers (about 3 s); succinctly's stack guard refuses with `exceeded maximum recursion depth` (ADR-0025). |
| `recursion-depth-100000` | timeout signal (10001 ms) | timeout signal (10008 ms) | by-design: Recursion 100000 deep: jq does not finish within 10 s; succinctly's stack guard refuses (ADR-0025). |
| `regex-gsub-large` | timeout signal (10007 ms) | ok 0 (33 ms) | reference-slow: `gsub("a";"b")` over 100000 characters: jq 1.7.1 does not finish within 10 s; succinctly answers in tens of milliseconds. |
| `array-set-too-huge-index` | crash signal (513 ms) | error 5 (22 ms) | reference-crash: `[] | .[1e12] = 1`: jq aborts (SIGSEGV); succinctly refuses the index with an error (exit 5, #5500). |
| `recursion-tail-100000` | timeout signal (10001 ms) | timeout signal (10009 ms) | by-design: Tail-position recursion 100000 deep: jq does not finish within 10 s; succinctly's stack guard refuses (ADR-0025), so it gets no tail-call elimination. |
| `mem-limit-64m-identity` | timeout signal (10006 ms) | ok 0 (45 ms) | reference-crash: Under `ulimit -v` 64 MiB, 1M-integer array: the reference jq 1.7.1 aborts; succinctly answers, on an evaluation stack sized to the cap (#5634). |
| `mem-limit-64m-string` | ok 0 (226 ms) | error 1 (12 ms) | by-design: Under `ulimit -v` 64 MiB a 20 MB string is read by jq but aborts succinctly on a failed allocation. A trivial run already maps about 42 MiB (the binary, the main thread's 8 MiB stack and the evaluation stack, 16 MiB at the least under a cap, #5634), and the document takes 28 MiB more: the input, and its index in two allocations of 2.5 MB and 5 MB. That is the semi-index kept whole beside the input, not a leak: it fits in 70 MiB on Linux aarch64. |
| `mem-limit-alloc-bomb` | timeout signal (10028 ms) | timeout signal (10033 ms) | by-design: `[range(1e8)] | length` under `ulimit -v` 512 MiB: jq 1.7.1 and succinctly both abort (killed by a signal, no exit status). Rust ends the process on a failed allocation (`memory allocation of N bytes failed`) where jq's `jv_mem_alloc` prints `cannot allocate memory` and aborts, so the output matches; a graceful error would need every container growth to be fallible. |
| `mem-limit-string-bomb` | crash signal (218 ms) | error 5 (7 ms) | reference-crash: `"a" * 1e9` under `ulimit -v` 512 MiB: jq 1.7.1 aborts; succinctly exits 5 with a graceful error. |

## D. Performance (process spawn, ms; matching outputs only)

Median of interleaved repetitions (21 requested, fewer at 100 MB; a row over 15 ms is topped up to 21 where the time allows), CV in parentheses; the tool order rotates each repetition. A speedup is reference ÷ succinctly, so below 1.00x jq is faster, and is a ratio of medians except where marked †: a row that long is moved by run-to-run noise, so its ratio is of each tool's fastest of the 21 runs, which the noise moves least (the times beside it stay medians). A row marked `CV>5%` is noise-dominated, and its ratio is not a finding on its own. `1.8.2 ÷ 1.7.1` is the secondary reference's own change in speed, always of medians.

## E. Memory (peak RSS and private memory, KiB; separate untimed runs, median of 3)

Peak RSS charges a process for the file-backed pages of its mapped executable and libraries, which are shared and reclaimable, so a larger binary reads higher on every row with the same heap (#5578). Private memory leaves them out: on Linux the largest `RssAnon` sampled while the process ran (a lower bound, and coarser for a run of a few milliseconds, so its ratios and the geomean carry the same caveat), on macOS the peak memory footprint. `n/a` where the platform offers neither.

## D/E. Piped stdin vs file argument

Each `*_stdin` query runs the program of the query before the suffix, with its input written to a pipe on stdin by the harness (read once into memory, then written from a thread, so there is no network and no slow producer) instead of named as a file argument. Whether the pipe changes what a tool costs is what the table measures: succinctly reads a file and stdin through different code (the evaluator's generic route), and the file-route figures above say nothing about it. Figures are medians of repetitions interleaved across the tools within a row; the file row and its stdin row are separate rows of one run, timed one after the other and not interleaved with each other, and each is gated on output identity like every other row. A ratio is stdin ÷ file, so above 1.00x the pipe is slower (or larger); a ratio over 1.25x is marked `>`. Memory is peak RSS and private memory of separate untimed runs, as above. A gap on a large compact input is mostly the pipe, not the evaluator: succinctly reads stdin to its end before it starts, so the time to move the bytes through a pipe is added to its run instead of overlapped with it, and the faster a query, the larger that is as a ratio (#6914 measured 100 MB into `cat` at 39 ms on the 7950X, against a 36 ms stdin gap on `users_field`). A `>` on a 1 MB row whose neighbours run the other way is the run's noise.

```bash
cargo build --release --features bench-runner
./target/release/succinctly dev compare jq --full
```
